stories.headline: Tamil Nadu man made thousands of ancient inscriptions searchable for free
stories.deck: Udhaya Shankar embarked on his journey by showcasing traditional kolam designs, but soon his focus shifted towards safeguarding Tamil inscriptions. Through his initiative, Udhayam.in, over 8,500 ancient texts have been made available for online searching. Balancing a design career, Shankar dedicates approximately six hours a day to this labor of love, showcasing his unwavering commitment to…
stories.bodyText:
Udhaya Shankar was quite young in 2007. It was the time when the internet was still juggling to find its place in everyday life of Indian people. But even then, Udhaya, a young designer from Tamil Nadu thought of an idea which was to showcase the traditional kolam designs to the world. And now, nearly 20 years later, that modest initiative has grown into something far more significant.
Udhaya, a full-time designer, has now created a digital platform that makes more than 8,500 ancient Tamil inscriptions searchable online. It is now helping students, researchers and history enthusiasts explore centuries of Tamil heritage.
A remarkable contribution
Udhaya’s contribution is quite significant and remarkable to heritage preservation which also earned him the THT Prof. S. Swaminathan Heritage Award 2026. Along with a citation, the recognition came with a cash prize of Rs 50,000. However, for Shankar, the real reward lies in making a part of India's history accessible to people who might otherwise never get an opportunity to explore it.
This is the story of Udhayam.in, the digital archive developed painstakingly.
A website that began with 500 kolam designs
M Udhaya Shankar (PC: Tamil Heritage Trust)
Shankar is an engineering graduate with a passion to create kolam patterns and wanted to share his work with the world. 
Around 2007, he had digitised several designs but lacked the technical knowledge to build a website.
He was then part of a Google group where he connected with its administrator. After hearing about Shankar's collection, the administrator offered to help. Within just five days, they created Udhayam.in.
How a font project turned into a heritage mission
Shankar's journey into epigraphy, the study of inscriptions, began when he received a request to create a font for Tamil-Brahmi, one of the earliest forms of the Tamil script.
But there was one problem which was he could not read Tamil-Brahmi at the time.
Instead of turning down the opportunity, he decided to learn. With the help of books recommended to him, he began studying the ancient script and comparing how its letters appeared across different inscriptions. He also travelled to various locations, photographed stone inscriptions and worked towards standardising the letterforms.
He then formed Adinatha Tamil-Brahmi font released in 2012
Making centuries of history accessible with a few clicks
Tamil script (Wiki)
Today, the website has information on more than 8,500 inscriptions, including Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions. Users can explore them through details such as their dates, geographical locations, dynasties and rulers. There is also an interactive map to help users locate inscriptions, along with image and word mapping features.
For Shankar, making the information accessible was only half the challenge. Ensuring its accuracy required years of painstaking research.
One of his biggest difficulties was identifying the present-day locations of inscriptions mentioned in decades-old publications. Village names, district boundaries and administrative divisions have changed over the years, making it difficult to establish where certain inscriptions were originally found.
In one instance, an old record identified an inscription's location as Kirumuttugur in the erstwhile North Arcot district. After an extensive search, Shankar traced it to present-day Kilumuttukur in Vellore district's KV Kuppam taluk.
Six hours every day, and a dream that needs support
M Udhaya Shankar
What makes Shankar's achievement particularly remarkable is that Udhayam.in is largely a one-person effort. He continues to work full-time as a designer at a private company while devoting an average of six hours every day to the heritage project.
The financial commitment is equally significant. According to him, maintaining the platform costs close to Rs 10 lakh annually, with nearly 90 per cent of the expenses funded from his own pocket. Donations, including contributions in kind such as laptops, and help from volunteers make up the remainder. He has also engaged a handful of students to assist with typing inscriptions.
Nearly 19 years after he first began sharing kolam designs online, the designer is now helping people discover stories etched in stone centuries ago.

stories.headline: Diktats, boycotts and the fight for rights
stories.deck: For over two years, 45 toddy-tapper and 10 Dalit families in Nizamabad’s Tallarampur have allegedly faced a complete social boycott for defying their Village Development Committee’s (VDC) orders. Denied access to groceries, medical aid and social gatherings, they have been pushed to the margins of everyday life. The growing clout of VDCs and nearly 90 complaints of alleged excesses before the…
stories.bodyText:
On a sunny afternoon last year, 40-year-old Kairi Kalyani dressed in her festive best and stepped out of her home with a plate of offerings, including turmeric, kumkum, flowers, coconuts and fruits. It was Sri Rama Navami, and Kalyani, along with a dozen other women from her neighbourhood in Tallarampur village of Nizamabad district, arrived at the local Ramalayam to perform kumkumarchana.
But what was meant to be a day of prayer and celebration quickly turned into an experience of humiliation. Just as the women settled among the other devotees, the temple priest allegedly asked them to leave. The reason? They belonged to the Goud (toddy-tapper) community and were not permitted to perform rituals at the temple!

stories.headline: Nearly 20 years after father’s death at sea, tragedy strikes Gujarati family again as sailor son killed in Oman attack
stories.bodyText: Ahmedabad: After nearly 20 years, a tragedy has once again struck the Gandhar family of Salaya village in Devbhumi Dwarka district. Their youngest member, a sailor, was killed when the vessel he was aboard was hit in an explosive projectile attack on an Indian-flagged cargo vessel in Oman near the Strait of Hormuz on November 2. Family members said that the victim, Nahim Ajij Gandhar, was among the 14 crew members aboard the vessel Al Jusufi, which was carrying 900 metric tonnes of dates from Hamriyah Port in the United Arab Emirates to Porbandar. The commercial vessel was reportedly struck by a drone or missile near Limah in Oman. Gandhar was killed in the attack, while the other 13 crew members survived. .Attack on vessel near Strait of Hormuz: Deceased sailor hailed from Gujarat, kin plan burial in Oman. "Some 20 or 21 years ago, Nahim's father Ajijbhai was also killed in the sea during a cyclone while returning from Dubai. He was also a sailor. His body was never recovered. The tragedy has struck the family once again," Irfan, cousin of Nahim at Salaya, told DH. He said Nahim was the youngest of five siblings. He has four sisters, all of whom are married, and an elder brother who works in the fishing industry in their village. According to Haji Akbar Sumbhaniya, who owned the ill-fated vessel, Nahim will be buried in Oman as his family was unable to travel to perform the last rites. "The visa process is long and there is no assurance from the government that it will be done sooner, considering the emergency. If we send the family, it will only delay the last rites. In our community, the dead are supposed to be buried as early as possible," Sumbhaniya told DH. He said that the survived crew members are trying to complete the procedure so that burial could take place sooner. He complained that the crew members were not getting any help from the Indian Embassy in Oman, rather one of the officials allegedly delayed the proceeding for 24 hours. "All the government does is big talks, promising to help after a crisis hits us. But in the end, we don't get anything. This is not the first time that our vessels have been destroyed since February this year," he said. He said that ever since the war broke out in West Asia, six vessels were completely destroyed. "We haven't received a single penny in assistance from the government. We are on our own. Neither our vessels nor our cargo nor our crew members are insured," he said. "The only exception was earlier in May when the Director General of Shipping gave Rs10 lakh to the family of Altaf Talab Ker, who died during a crossfire in Strait of Hormuz," Sumbhaniya added.

stories.headline: Maharashtra Government makes provision for ₹160 crore in 2026-27 Budget for development of primitive tribes
stories.deck: The package includes 130 crore reserved for primitive tribes, ₹30 crore reserved for the Pardhi community, and also provides for 100% government grant for individual and collective benefit schemes
stories.bodyText:
Under ‘Viksit Maharashtra 2047’, the Maharashtra Government made provision for a special package of ₹160 crore in the 2026-27 Budget for the “holistic development of the primitive tribes” — Katkari, Kolam and Madia — along with the Pardhi community.
The package includes 130 crore reserved for primitive tribes, ₹30 crore reserved for the Pardhi community, and also provides for 100% government grant for individual and collective benefit schemes.
The ₹130 crore will be further divided and allocated as follows: ₹100 crore for basic amenities and ₹30 crore for individual and collective benefit schemes. For the Pardhi community, ₹10 crore will be allocated for basic amenities and ₹20 crore for individual and collective benefit schemes.
The announcement to provide funds through a special package for the holistic development of primitive communities was made in the 2026-27 Budget.
The State Government issued a Government Resolution (GR) on 2 November 2026 to implement the package.
The minimum grant of ₹50,000 will be given for an individual scheme, and up to a maximum of ₹7.5 lakh for a collective scheme of two or more beneficiaries.
“If beneficiaries are deprived of benefits under schemes of other departments because they are unable to pay their own share, then the Tribal Development Department will chip in. Greater encouragement will be given to the formation of women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) for women’s empowerment, enabling women to take up collective ventures and achieve economic empowerment of their families, groups will be given grants of up to ₹7.5 lakh,” stated in a CMO statement.
The funds will also be used to organise awareness drives and special camps, providing essential documents like Aadhaar Card, Voter ID Card, Ration Card, Caste Certificate, MGNREGA Job Card, Ayushman Card and Bank Account. Health check-up camps, visits by Anganwadi workers, ASHA workers and nurses, health education and benefits of government health schemes will also be provided.
The package also includes increasing student attendance, bringing out-of-school children into the mainstream of education, and organising residential camps in Ashram Schools during summer for children of migrant families.

briefs.headline: Trump team stands firm: Rubio rules out exit, Hegseth gets president's backing
briefs.deck: Marco Rubio has dismissed rumors about potentially leaving his position in the Trump administration. He asserts that completing Trump's second term has always been his plan. While he supports Vice President JD Vance for a future presidential run, Rubio avoids discussing his ambitions. Reports regarding a possible exit have been rejected by the White House and the State Department.
briefs.bodyText:
US secretary of state 
Marco Rubio
 has dismissed reports that he is considering leaving the Trump administration following the Republican Party's setbacks in the midterm elections, saying that completing President Donald Trump's second term has “always been my plan”.
In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio rejected speculation that he might step down ahead of a possible 2028 presidential campaign and declined to discuss his political ambitions.
“Working for President Trump until the end of his term has always been my plan,” Rubio said, adding that he did not know where reports about his possible departure had originated.
“I love the work I’m doing,” he said. “And plus I always laugh when they say he’s going to leave his job. I go, ‘Which one?’”
Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, refused to entertain questions about whether he was considering a presidential run in 2028.
“I literally will not talk about 2028 anymore,” he told the newspaper in his White House office. “I just won’t do it.”
Rubio backs JD Vance for 2028 presidential race
Rubio has previously indicated that he would support Vice President JD Vance if he decided to run for president in 2028.
“JD is a very good friend of mine,” Rubio told NBC News in May. “If JD runs for president, I think he’d be a phenomenal candidate. I’ve said publicly, and I’ll say it again, I’ll be the first person to sign up and support him.”
However, Vance's post-election assessment on Wednesday included criticism of the administration's approach to the Iran war, its policy on Israel and its messaging on the economy.
The vice-president blamed the war with Iran for the Republicans' election setbacks and said voters had turned against the administration's position on Israel and its handling of economic concerns. Trump has closely aligned himself with Israel and dismissed concerns over affordability as a “hoax”.
Asked whether he agreed with Vance's assessment, Rubio initially deflected, saying he was not “really involved in domestic politics”.
However, Rubio acknowledged the political implications of the Iran war when he appeared alongside Trump at a rally in Kansas on Sunday. Trump praised the secretary of state and joked that he might have to fire him because he had become “too popular”.
Explaining his presence at the rally, Rubio said he was travelling with the president as the designated national security official. He also acknowledged Trump's remarks that the war had been a factor in the election results.
“Higher prices at the gas pump, I acknowledge, is not like the kind of thing you campaign on and brag about,” Rubio said.
However, he defended Trump's decision to take action despite its potential political costs, saying the president “deserves a tremendous amount of credit” for doing what he considered necessary.
“Ultimately, that is the price of leadership — is the willingness to do things that may not be politically popular or expedient but are necessary for your country and its long-term future,” he said.
White House rejects reports of Rubio's possible exit
The White House and the State Department have also rejected reports that Rubio could leave his position following the Republican setbacks.
White House spokesperson Beni Rae Harmony described the reports as a fabricated hoax circulated by anonymous sources, while assistant secretary of state for global public affairs Dylan Johnson called them baseless fake news.
The speculation over a possible administration shake-up has also involved defence secretary 
Pete Hegseth
, whose handling of the Iran war has drawn criticism following the election losses.
The White House has denied reports that Hegseth and Rubio might leave their positions. Trump told ABC News that he had received calls about Hegseth but had “every intention” of keeping him. He later praised the defence secretary, saying he had “done a fantastic job”.
However, Republican Representative Thomas Massie has said he intends to move ahead with an effort to impeach Hegseth, with a resolution expected as early as next week. Hegseth has rejected the effort, describing it as a politically motivated attempt to undermine him.
Separately, The Washington Post reported that Trump could be considering replacing General Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command.
Both have played significant roles in providing guidance on the Iran war.

briefs.headline: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
briefs.deck: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths
briefs.bodyText:
Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme. And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

briefs.headline: Delhi air quality worsens, AQI hits 389 as several areas turn ‘severe’
briefs.deck: Delhi continues to experience high pollution levels as the overall Air Quality Index reaches 389. Several areas, including IIT Delhi and Rohini, reported even worse levels in the 'severe' category. Local residents are expressing discomfort due to the deteriorating air quality, reporting issues like breathing difficulties and eye irritation. The Delhi Environment Minister has attributed the…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Delhi continued to reel under high pollution levels on Friday, with the city’s overall 
Air Quality Index
 (AQI) recorded at 389 in the ‘very poor’ category at 8 am, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
Several areas in the national capital reported AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category. IIT Delhi and Rohini recorded an AQI of 474 each, followed by Punjabi Bagh at 465, RK Puram at 443, ITO at 422, Firoz Shah Road at 420 and India Gate at 403, according to CPCB data.
Meanwhile, municipal authorities deployed truck-mounted water sprinklers around India Gate to carry out water sprinkling operations under Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).
Other areas also reported high pollution levels. Anand Vihar and Akshardham recorded an AQI of 359, while IGI Airport Terminal 3 registered 385. The AQI stood at 393 in Aya Nagar and 391 in Chandni Chowk.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi recorded a minimum morning temperature of 17.8°C, with skies remaining mainly clear. The weather department has forecast shallow fog over the next four days, followed by fog or mist during early morning hours on November 10 and 11.
Residents continued to report discomfort due to the deteriorating air quality. A local resident, Sarvesh, said the pollution had made breathing difficult and was causing irritation in the eyes.
"It's causing a lot of problems. As you can see, it's morning, and there isn't much traffic, but because of the pollution, it's hard to breathe, and I'm feeling anxious. There's a lot of smog, making it feel like the middle of January. So, there are a lot of issues, like a burning sensation in the eyes," he said.
Another local, Nemichand Sharma, said that the crisis feels like the predictable consequence of unchecked urbanisation and administrative apathy.
"I am seventy-one years old now. And ever since Delhi has developed, the progress and development in the name of development has brought about a huge increase in pollution. They have been given a free pass: wherever dirt is going to spread, just let it spread. Do whatever you want. And every day, instead of showing the pollution from Akshardham and solving the problem, governments are doing nothing with all their machinery except making money in the name of pollution. There is no ground-level work to end pollution," he said.
Earlier on Thursday, Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa accused Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann of misleading people over paddy harvesting and stubble burning. Sirsa said stubble burning in Punjab had contributed significantly to the deteriorating air quality in the national capital.
Addressing the media at the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) in Shastri Park, Sirsa claimed that 77% of the stubble had already been burnt, citing data from the Punjab government.
"Yesterday, Bhagwant Mann held a press conference and falsely claimed that the harvesting of paddy has not yet begun; however, according to the data provided by his own government, 77 per cent of the stubble (parali) has already been burnt," he said.
(With Agency Inputs)

briefs.headline: From Madeira, Manchester, Madrid to immortality: CR7 walks off, into people's hearts
briefs.deck: Before Ronaldo, a senior Portugal side had never won anything, had only made the World Cup semifinals twice, in 1966 and 2006 (his first World Cup). With him leading them, they won three trophies in nine years.
briefs.bodyText:
The iconic 'Siu' celebration will no longer ring out on the international stage. Not all curtain calls are happy spectacles, a packed arena cheering the last hurrah of a performer par excellence. Cristiano Ronaldo had his floodlit moments in the cauldrons of Stade de France, Porto, Gelsenkirchen, Luzhniki, Wembley, the Bernabeu or Munich's Allianz Arena.
On Thursday, Portugal's superstar announced his intention to retire from the country's national team in a social media post, bringing an end to one of the most illustrious careers in all football history. "The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team," he wrote in an 866-word message. "I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.
"Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future ... A journey that began in Aug 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end. When I look back at everything with the national team, I don't just see the matches, goals, records or trophies."
All expected him to say ‘obrigado’ at Dallas Stadium after Portugal lost to Spain in his last World Cup match on July 6, 2026. It marked his 27th appearance across a record six tournaments (2006-2026), making him the oldest player in a World Cup knockout match at 41.
Instead, the Portugal great, if not the greatest, waited for his bete noire Lionel Messi to sail into the twilight at the Monumental Stadium, waited till national coach Jorge Jesus’ royal ignore forced him into an ugly spat, a chase to the airport to coax him back. Of late, Cristiano had been making headlines for the wrong reasons.
Images of Cristiano struggling inside the rival penalty box have long overshadowed his overwhelming prowess that made him snatch five Ballons D’Or to Messi’s eight. Their game of one-upmanship spread across two decades leaving the world gasping for more. Gen Z is cleaved down the middle over the Portuguese and the Argentinian. The discourse will take some years to lose steam.
No men’s footballer has made as many international appearances (234) or scored as many goals (146) for their nation as Ronaldo. As a testament to his longevity — 94 of them came after his 30th birthday.
The five-time Ballon d’Or-winner made his international debut in 2003, and won the 2016 European Championship, in addition to two Nations League titles, with Portugal.
Ronaldo scored three goals at this summer’s World Cup as his nation exited in the Round of 16.
Recalling his great matches would be an exercise in academic drudgery. The hat-trick against Spain in Sochi in 2018 and the World Cup qualifier goals against Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s Sweden in 2013 are just the tip of the iceberg.
So are the moments of irony. In 2012, Luis Nani missed one on a platter offered to him by Cristiano in the Euro semifinal against Spain. Portugal lost. Four years later, Cristiano’s final against France ended in a tear-soaked heartache, injured and substituted after 25 minutes. Portugal went on to win their first continental title.
Before Ronaldo, a senior Portugal side had never won anything, had only made the World Cup semifinals twice, in 1966 and 2006 (his first World Cup). With him leading them, they won three trophies in nine years.
Madeira, his birthplace, has a museum as a tribute to its most famous son. Like Santos has one for Pele.
Accolades will continue to flow and the ‘Siuuu’ celebration will be replicated by boys across the globe for years to come.
For now, like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and currently sits on 985. The immortal longings refuse to die.
As his goodbye post reads: “Goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people’s hearts.”

briefs.headline: Sarah Jukaku: First Muslim U.S. senator’s wife has a Karnataka link
briefs.deck: Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
briefs.bodyText:
Sarah Jukaku, a doctor and wife of Democrat Abdul EI-Sayed, who is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate in the midterm elections, traces her family roots to Bhatkal in Uttara Kannada district, of Karnataka, according to media reports.
Dr. Sarah is the granddaughter of the late J.H. Shamsuddin Jukaku, a lawyer from Bhatkal who served as Deputy Finance Minister in the erstwhile Mysore State government, led by the then Chief Minister B.D. Jatti, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Shamsuddin was also the Deputy Minister for Electricity in the then government led by then Chief Minister S. Nijalingappa, reports said.
It is said that following the death of Shamsuddin, his family members shifted to different parts of India, including to Bengaluru.

Reports said that Dr. Sarah is the daughter of Jukaku S. Tayeb, also a doctor, who was among four sons of Shamsuddin, who also had six daughters. Dr. Tayeb moved to the U.S. in the 1980s.
They said that Dr. Sarah met EI-Sayed in the University of Michigan and they got married in 2006. Reports said that their family has still maintained relations with family members in India.

briefs.headline: Buyers want bang for the buck as green crackers fail to deliver
briefs.deck: Traders say delayed licences have squeezed the window of sale, while confusion over green crackers persists as buyers continue to expect the familiar loud bangs of conventional fireworks.
briefs.bodyText:
Light travels faster than sound. Across Hyderabad, brightly lit firecracker stalls have sprung up ahead of Deepavali, their colourful displays drawing attention in several pockets of the city. Large makeshift tents lined with rows of fireworks have come up at designated locations, with fire extinguishers and other safety measures in place. Traders are preparing for the festive rush, but some say business has been slower than in previous years, even as the market undergoes a gradual shift towards green crackers.
Green crackers, developed as a less polluting alternative to conventional fireworks, are intended to reduce emissions and noise. Their adoption has gathered pace over the past few years, with several established brands moving towards greener variants. However, the transition has also brought a change in the sound and performance that customers have traditionally associated with firecrackers.
Sanjay Kumar Gupta of Ramamurthy Trading Company, which has been in the business since 1975, said many customers were still unaware of the distinction between green and conventional crackers. Some mistake the comparatively lower sound levels of green crackers for a decline in quality, he said.
“For customers, Deepavali is synonymous with crackers, blasts and bangs. They expect that familiar sound. When green crackers do not make a loud bang like traditional ones, they assume that the quality of established brands has gone down,” he said. Another trader said some customers even returned to complain about the sound, believing that the crackers were not performing as expected.
Myakala Venugopal of Shivashakti Agency, who has been in the business for 30 years, said the range of green crackers had expanded considerably. Even fancy fireworks, which were earlier not available in green variants, were now being manufactured as green crackers. Customers who are more conscious of environmental concerns specifically ask for them, he said.
Raghavendra of Hyderabad Crackers in Kukatpally said the shift towards green crackers began around 2021, with popular brands gradually moving to green variants. Their packaging now carries the green symbol, he said. While some fancy fireworks have stopped being produced, even the classic mirchi bombs now produce less sound and smoke.
He said the quality and packaging of green crackers had improved this year, with a majority of customers asking for them. However, a lack of awareness about the green crackers initiative continued to result in complaints from some buyers.
Several customers are also opting to place bulk orders directly with manufacturers in Sivakasi, including Standard Fireworks, at wholesale rates. “I have two children, and every Deepavali we invite my nieces, nephews and other relatives home to celebrate together. It has become a family tradition, so we need a large quantity of crackers. Buying directly from manufacturers in Sivakasi works out cheaper than purchasing them in smaller quantities from retail stalls,” said Ravi Kumar, a resident of Kowkoor.
Licence delays add to traders’ concerns
For traders, the challenges this season have extended beyond changing customer preferences. Gupta said he applied for a licence around 20 days ago but received it only on November 5, four days before the festival. He said receiving licences at least 10 days before the festival would make a considerable difference to businesses.
“We are now hoping to break even, not even make a profit. Earlier, we did not have even a minute of free time. Now it is 8.30 p.m. and I am sitting idle and talking to you, with just four or five customers looking around the stall. Families involved in this business struggle throughout the year to deal with the losses during this season,” he said.

briefs.headline: MSRTC announces ₹10,000 ex-gratia grant for 83,000 officers
briefs.deck: The decision, taken at a meeting of MSRTC officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), also includes an advance payment of ₹12,500 for eligible employees and an increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) from 58% to 60%
briefs.bodyText:
Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has announced a ₹10,000 ex-gratia grant for each of the 83,000 officers and employees of the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC).
The decision, taken at a meeting of MSRTC officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), also includes an advance payment of ₹12,500 for eligible employees and an increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) from 58% to 60%.
“Despite the financial difficulties faced by the MSRTC, employees should not be deprived of the joy of Diwali,” Mr. Sarnaik said. He added that the measures would impose an additional financial burden of around ₹160 crore on the Corporation. However, he said, employees’ efforts to provide safe transport services to lakhs of passengers needed to be rewarded.

briefs.headline: 'Vote red today!' Elon Musk deletes pro-Republican posts after spending $458 million
briefs.deck: Elon Musk removed social media posts encouraging support for Republican candidates after Democrats achieved significant victories. His pinned message included a call to vote Republican on Election Day. Musk’s financial backing totaled around $458 million, making him a significant donor during the election cycle. The election results also caused a decline in Musk's personal wealth and the stock…
briefs.bodyText:
Elon Musk
 has deleted social media posts urging voters to support Republican candidates in the US midterm elections, after Democrats made significant gains and secured control of both chambers of Congress.
The removed posts included a pinned October 29 message calling on voters to elect Republican senators and an Election Day appeal stating “Vote red today!”. According to Forbes, Musk took down the pinned post early Wednesday, around the time Democrat James Talarico claimed victory in the Texas Senate race.
The news agency Associated Press called the Texas contest for Talarico shortly after 11 pm EST on Tuesday, confirming the defeat of Republican Ken Paxton, who had received substantial financial backing from Musk.
Musk's chatbot Grok also confirmed the deletion after an X user asked whether he was removing posts related to the election. “True,” Grok replied late Wednesday morning, saying Musk had deleted the “Vote red today!” message after the results showed “major Republican losses”.
The Election Day appeal was among Musk's few direct interventions on the platform urging support for Republicans.
It had appeared alongside posts promoting Grok and a message featuring a raised-eyebrow emoji in response to Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who also won his Senate race.
Musk jokes about election losses, comments on voter ID
Musk was more active on X on Wednesday morning, sharing several posts analysing the election results and making sarcastic remarks about the Republican defeats.
“Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time 🤷♂️,” he wrote in one post, shortly after saying, “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.”
He also responded to a post claiming that voters had agreed with Republicans on every policy issue but had still voted Democrat, writing: “Voter ID failed in California.”
The remark referred to the defeat of a California ballot measure that would have required voters to show government-issued photo identification when casting ballots in person or provide identification numbers when voting by mail.
Musk subsequently returned to posting about his technology ventures, including Starlink and Grok, according to The Daily Beast and Futurism.
Musk spent hundreds of millions backing Republicans
Musk was among the biggest financial backers of Republican candidates and aligned political causes during the midterm election cycle.
He channelled at least $458 million into Republican-aligned causes, making him the largest individual donor in modern US political history during the election cycle.
Federal Election Commission filings and other reporting cited by the publication showed that a significant portion, around $216 million, went directly to his super PAC, America PAC.
The organisation financed voter turnout operations, ground-level campaigning and targeted digital advertising. Musk increased his spending during the second half of the election cycle, seeking to help Republicans retain control of Congress.
His contributions went heavily towards the Texas Senate contest, the Senate Leadership Fund and key House battlegrounds in New York, New Jersey and Iowa.
According to Federal Election Commission data, Musk's spending through super PACs and other individual contributions stood around $474 million. The New York Times estimated that he spent approximately $224 million in Texas alone.
106 House and Senate candidates had received Musk's backing. As of around noon EST on Wednesday, 19 had won, all in seats Republicans were expected to retain, while 47 had lost and 40 contests remained uncalled.
Tesla, SpaceX shares fall as Musk's wealth declines
The election results also coincided with a fall in the value of Musk's companies and his personal wealth.
Forbes estimated Musk's net worth at $878 billion on Wednesday, after it fell by $23.7 billion during the morning as markets reacted to the prospect of a Democratic-controlled Congress.
Shares of Tesla and SpaceX declined, amid concerns about a possible regulatory slowdown in data centre construction. Dell, Nvidia and SoftBank also recorded notable declines.
Tesla shares fell 3.3% and SpaceX shares dropped 3.8%, wiping out more than $120 billion in value, according to Bloomberg. The publication cited a Financial Times estimate that Musk had lost around $30 billion in personal wealth.
The losses followed a costly election cycle in which Musk had sought to replicate his support for candidates backed by Donald Trump in the 2024 election.
According to OpenSecrets, Musk spent about $291 million during that earlier cycle.

stories.headline: From ghee masala dosa to Mysore pak, Bengaluru’s favourite foods set to cost more
stories.deck: Prices of items like ghee masala dosa, kesari bath, upma, pongal, ghee rice, bisibele bath, rotis, naans, parottas and sweets like halwa will also be increased”
stories.bodyText:
Following the increase in the prices of ghee, butter and paneer, hotel associations and sweet shops will also be increasing the prices of sweets and food items in which ghee, butter and paneer are used.
Veerendra Kamat, secretary, Bangalore Hotels Association, said, “Ghee, butter and paneer prices were increased a day ago. Before that, milk and curd prices had increased. Hence, tea and coffee prices in all hotels across the city, from small to big ones, have increased by ₹3 to ₹5. Now prices of items like ghee masala dosa, kesari bath, upma, pongal, ghee rice, bisibele bath, rotis, naans, parottas and sweets like halwa will also be increased.”
Mr. Kamat added, “An average price of ghee masala dosa is ₹120 to ₹130 across most of the hotels, which will be increased up to ₹125 to ₹135. Some premium hotels charge up to ₹200 also. Other items like kesari bath, ghee rice, pongal and bisibele bath will also be increased by ₹5. We cannot increase these prices beyond ₹5 because customers will stop coming and the entire business will be impacted.”
He also clarified that the association cannot set a standard price for all the hotels. “Hoteliers price the dishes as per the location of the hotel, customer footfall, scale of business, and profit and loss, which is calculated at the end of every month,” he added.
Sweets to also cost dear
Meanwhile, Madhu Iyengar, general secretary, Karnataka Bakeries, Sweets and Cafe Association (KBSCA), said, “When prices of milk and curds had increased, we thought to continue selling sweets on the same scale or price.But the ghee price hike has impacted our budgets too. Since it is the festival season, where we aim to make good business, we have not increased prices of any sweet where milk and ghee are used. However, we will increase the price probably in December during the off-season by 3% to 5%.”
Arjun P., a manager working at a famous sweet outlet that has branches across the city, said, “In our shop, special Mysore Pak made using ghee is priced at ₹473 for 500 grams, and Kaju Katli at ₹700 for 500 grams. Mango barfi and doodh pedha are probably the lowest, priced around ₹419 for 500 grams. Kesar peda is priced at ₹473 for 500 grams. When the prices are hiked in December or during New Year, all these will be increased by ₹5 to ₹10.”
Households feel the pinch
Apart from hotels and sweet shops, households have also felt the heat of the price rise, especially during Deepavali. Prathiba Reddy, a resident of Ramamurthy Nagar, said, “People are yet to recover from the milk and curd price hike, and the government has gone ahead to increase ghee, paneer and butter prices. During the festival, I use ghee for most of the items, either to fry or mix it with maida and wheat flour for making snacks and sweets. A one-litre sachet of Nandini ghee has gone up by almost ₹135.”
Expressing disappointment over the price hike of essential commodities, Manjunath M., a gig worker, said, “Festivals are not for poor people like us who earn less than ₹20,000 a month and have five people in a family to look after. The milk and ghee price hike have impacted a working-class person like me.”

stories.headline: Karnataka voter lists show duplicates, errors after special intensive revision revision
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Months after the special intensive revision (SIR) was billed as a clean-up of electoral rolls, voters across 
Karnataka
 are finding the final rolls riddled with duplicate entries, garbled names, incorrect ages, and incomplete addresses.
“My family had applied for a new voter ID the year before SIR. When the final rolls came in, our names were listed twice in the same booth,” said a voter from Karnataka. “How two entries made it to the final list is a mystery.”
Hers is one of over 1,000 such cases in a single Bengaluru constituency, according to MP 
Mansoor Ali Khan
, who had earlier flagged instances of “vote chori” in Mahadevapura. He said the duplicates have now carried over to the final SIR rolls.
Election officials were unreachable for comment on how duplicates made it to the rolls, for which 5.5 crore voters went through re-verification and 43 lakh had to submit documents to prove their eligibility.
A 
TOI
 review of the voter lists showed that addresses against several names were missing, with full stops or hyphens in their place. In some cases, arbitrary numbers that appeared on the draft list were carried forward to the final list.
Officials on the ground attribute this to transliteration and data-entry errors, and say Form 8 may be needed for rectification. However, there has been no official announcement on how such issues will be addressed.
Names have also been mangled. Despite receiving a notice and responding to it, a voter named ‘Adrian’ found his name listed as ‘Aatriyana’, raising questions about the purpose of the rectification process.
Another voter said her name was misspelt in the enumeration form even though her older voter ID had it right. “I filled the third column that asked for our recent details, and yet the wrong spelling was retained. How come the details we filled in the third part of the form have not been considered for the final list?” she asked.
Ages are also off. Voters across the state report being assigned ages greater than their actual ages. “I’ve been marked three years older than my age right now,” said a voter from Mangaluru. Similar cases were reported in Bengaluru.
Cabinet asks CM to take a call on rolls
Times News Network
Bengaluru: The state govt is yet to decide whether electoral rolls prepared after SIR should be used for upcoming local body elections, with the issue triggering an hour-long discussion at the cabinet meeting Thursday.
The cabinet authorised CM 
DK Shivakumar
 to consult the Congress high command and take a decision on the matter.
According to sources, some ministers favoured using the final electoral rolls published recently after completion of SIR exercise. They argued that the revision had been conducted systematically in Karnataka, with only minor discrepancies compared to other states. Others, however, favoured using the rolls prepared by Election Commission of India (ECI) before SIR.
Rural development and panchayat raj (RDPR) minister Eshwar B Khandre said the cabinet discussed the issue and several opinions were expressed. He said state election commission will take a final call on which electoral rolls should be used for local body elections.

briefs.headline: This weekend, Deepavali getaway rush will test Bengaluru’s roads as massive vehicle outflow expected
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Brace for a 
Deepavali
 getaway rush on major roads as lakhs of Bengalureans prepare to hit the highways from Friday morning, triggering what traffic police expect to be one of the biggest festive outflows from the city. With families heading to their native places to celebrate the festival, traffic is expected to swell sharply along key exit corridors, including Tumakuru Road, Mysuru Road and Hosur Road. Traffic police anticipate the rush to surpass the congestion witnessed during the recent Dasara holidays.
In anticipation of a massive surge in vehicular flow, authorities are gearing up for a two-day traffic management exercise, with additional personnel being deployed at critical junctions and bottlenecks. From as early as Friday morning, cops will focus on clearing illegal parking along major stretches, including Yeshwantpur, Kengeri and Hosur Main Road, to ensure smoother traffic movement and maintain lane discipline. Personnel deployment at key choke points is expected to be increased threefold to tackle the rush.
The biggest challenge, however, is expected to unfold from Friday evening, when thousands of 
KSRTC
 and private buses begin ferrying passengers out of the city in different directions. 
“The real challenge begins when more buses — both KSRTC and private — start leaving Bengaluru in different directions from the evening. This time, the rush will be more than that during Dasara as more people will celebrate Deepavali. They will travel to hometowns across north and central Karnataka, Mysuru and coastal Karnataka,” a senior traffic police officer said.
Police estimate that more than 5,000 long-distance buses could leave the city on Friday evening and night alone. Goraguntepalya junction, a major transit point for buses heading towards north, central and coastal Karnataka, is expected to bear the brunt. As against the usual daily movement of 600 to 800 buses, the number is expected to be 2,500 to 3,000.
Congestion is also likely to spill over to the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) route, adding to the pressure on Bengaluru’s already stretched road network. Police have advised commuters to avoid major bottlenecks such as Goraguntepalya during peak night hours and plan their journeys accordingly.
Haunting Dasara gridlock
Traffic officials are keen to avoid a repeat of the nightmarish gridlock witnessed during the Dasara holiday exodus, when thousands of vehicles and long-distance buses crawled towards the city’s outskirts. During the rush, several buses took 5-6 hours just to exit Bengaluru, with traffic congestion continuing until nearly 2.30am.
The Goraguntepalya-Tumakuru Road stretch was one of the worst bottlenecks. Buses leaving Majestic were held up for 3-4 hours on the relatively short stretch leading to Goraguntepalya. Commuters reported that the journey from Orion Mall to Govardhan Theatre took over 2.5 hours, while several buses reached Nagasandra only around 2am!

briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: For years, multiplexes have faced criticism over the exorbitant prices they charge for food and beverages. Recently, a customer at a city multiplex was left flabbergasted after allegedly discovering that disposable cups were being reused to serve already expensive drinks.
The incident came to light Thursday after Mithil, an Instagram user, shared a video clip claiming that his son’s cricket coach had encountered the issue at PVR Cinemas in Forum South Mall on Kanakapura Road.
In the video, the customer is seen confronting multiplex staff over a stack of disposable cups that allegedly contained remnants of a soft drink. Initially, a staff member denies that the cups were already used. The customer, however, persists and demands to speak to the manager, who also denies the allegation. Although the staff offer to replace the cup and serve him a fresh beverage, the customer refuses. The video has garnered over 1.2 million views.
Responding to it, Forum South Mall apologised to the customer and said the matter was being looked into. “The PVR team is currently investigating the matter, and appropriate action will be taken to ensure this is addressed,” the mall stated in its Instagram response.
The incident has triggered widespread criticism from netizens, with many questioning the multiplex’s hygiene standards, particularly given the high prices charged for food and beverages. “The worst part is that they actually charge us for that used glass (sic) also,” one user commented. Another said, “This is after paying Rs 400-500 per glass (sic) for a Rs 40 beverage.”
Several users also raised concerns about the potential health risks of reusing disposable cups. “Imagine if the previous person who drank has a contagious health issue!” another user commented.
Some users speculated that the alleged practice could be aimed at cutting operational costs and improving profit margins. Others urged moviegoers to crush disposable cups and plates before discarding them in public places, suggesting that this would prevent them from being reused.

briefs.headline: Festive treats get dearer as Karnataka Milk Federation hikes ghee, butter and paneer prices

Bengaluru: Festive meals and must-have sweets are set to leave a bitter taste with Karnataka Cooperative Milk Producers’ Federation (KMF) increasing ghee prices by Rs 135 a kg and butter prices by Rs 140 a kg, besides a sharp rise in paneer price.
The immediate price revision comes within a week of govt increasing milk and curd prices, and also bus fares. Following multiple hikes, sweetmeat shops, bakeries, hotels and restaurants were already gearing up for passing on a part of the additional burden to customers — likely by 15%.
Traditional delicacies such as Mysore Pak, Dharwad Peda, laddoo, halwa and Kaju Katli depend on pure ghee, which accounts for nearly 40-50% of the raw material cost in several preparations. “Customers may have to pay Rs 75-150 more per kg for traditional ghee-based sweets across retail counters,” said Suresh Chandra, a sweet-maker in Bengaluru.
Restaurants and hotels, too, are preparing for price revision. Benne dosa, ghee masala dosa, ghee rice and ghee idli are likely to become costlier by Rs 15-25 per plate across darshinis and casual dining outlets. The price shock could extend to KMF’s own festive offerings. 
Its popular Nandini Mysore Pak and peda boxes may also see revised price tags.
With Nandini paneer prices jumping from Rs 408 to Rs 485 a kg, popular dishes such as paneer butter masala, shahi paneer, kadai paneer and paneer tikka are expected to become more expensive, according to hoteliers.
The dessert section, too, may be affected. Ghee gulab jamun, kheer and other premium milk-based desserts, along with lassi, butter cakes and pastries, could witness price increases of 10-15%, industry representatives said.
“We are caught between rising input costs and customer resistance. Ghee and paneer are essential ingredients for maintaining authentic taste and quality. Given the unprecedented increase in KMF prices, passing on at least part of the additional burden to consumers has become unavoidable,” said Veerendra Kamath, secretary of Bruhat Bangalore Hotels’ Association.

briefs.headline: Karnataka government’s fare hike on electric buses questioned as commuters flag diesel price rationale
briefs.deck: BMTC officials say fares are determined uniformly across the corporation and are not calculated according to the fuel consumed by individual buses
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government’s decision to increase fares across Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) services has drawn criticism from commuters, who have questioned the rationale for citing rising diesel prices to justify the hike, particularly when a portion of the corporation’s fleet now comprises electric buses.
The issue has gained attention in the context of the Gross Cost Contract (GCC) model, under which electric buses are operated by private contractors. Commuters have pointed out that several conventional diesel buses, particularly on Vayu Vajra services connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport, have been replaced with electric buses. They have questioned why passengers using these services should also bear the burden of a fare revision primarily attributed to increasing diesel costs.
“Inconsistent”
Jagan Desai, a BMTC commuter from Vijayanagar, said that the decision appeared inconsistent with the government’s efforts to promote electric mobility and encourage people to use public transport. “The government has spent years encouraging people to embrace electric public transport as part of its efforts to tackle Bengaluru’s worsening air pollution and traffic congestion. However, increasing fares on services operated by electric buses sends a contradictory message. These vehicles do not depend on diesel, yet their passengers are also being asked to pay more,” he said.
He added that Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh had attributed the fare revision to a ₹10.47 increase in diesel prices since May. “While the increase in fuel prices may have affected the corporation’s diesel-operated services, applying the same justification to electric buses raises questions about the basis for the revision. Passengers are being asked to pay higher fares even on services that are not directly affected by diesel price fluctuations,” he said.
According to BMTC figures, 1,779 buses are operating under the GCC model in Bengaluru. Against the corporation’s total fleet of 6,907 buses, including electric, diesel, and BS-VI vehicles, these account for approximately 25.7% of its fleet.
Different fares idea mooted
Another commuter, Srinivas Babu from Sanjaynagar, questioned why the corporation could not consider a separate fare structure for electric buses. “With electric buses forming a part of BMTC’s fleet, the corporation should at least examine whether passengers using these services can be charged lower fares. If the objective of introducing electric buses is to promote cleaner and more sustainable public transport, commuters should also experience some benefit from that transition. Why should passengers travelling in buses that do not use diesel pay the same increased fares as those travelling in conventional fuel-powered buses?” he asked.
BMTC defends hike
However, BMTC officials have defended the decision, stating that fares are determined uniformly across the corporation and are not calculated according to the fuel used by individual buses.
An official said that the corporation functioned as an integrated transport system, with expenditure extending beyond fuel costs to include staff salaries, maintenance, infrastructure and other operational liabilities. “BMTC does not maintain separate ticket rates for diesel and electric buses. Revenue collected across different services and vehicle categories is pooled together to meet the corporation’s overall expenditure. Any operational savings achieved through electric buses also contribute to meeting costs on other routes, including services that continue to operate with conventional fuel-powered vehicles,” the official said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka HC issues notice on plea against Disabilities Commissioner appointment
briefs.bodyText:
The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered notice to the State government on a petition challenging the appointment of Venkataramanaswamy S.V. as the State Commissioner for Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
Justice S. Sunil Dutt Yadav passed the order on the petition filed by Praveen Ullagaddi, a 43-year-old advocate and disability rights activist from Belagavi, who has 80% permanent locomotor disability.
The petitioner, who was an aspirant to the post, termed the selection process “opaque, arbitrary and non-transparent.” Dr. Venkataramanaswamy was appointed to the post on October 31.
It has been stated in the petition that the post fell vacant on March 5, 2026, and was advertised on March 7 in English and Kannada newspapers pursuant to Section 79 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. The petitioner, who is the president of the State Divyan Para-Valley Association of Karnataka and a two-term vice-president of the Karnataka State Association for Physically Handicapped, applied on April 4.
The petition states that nearly 47 applications were received and that a search-cum-selection committee was constituted under Rule 31 of the Karnataka State Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2019. However, the petitioner claims he was never informed of subsequent selection proceedings or given any explanation for his non-selection.
“The entire process of the appointment is shrouded in mystery,” the petitioner claimed, while complaining that there was no disclosure of the committee’s composition, the shortlisting criteria, or the basis for selecting the appointee.
The petitioner contends that the selection violates Rule 31, which mandates a panel of three suitable candidates recommended by the committee, comprising at least one disabled member or caregiver. He argues that the appointment offends Article 14 of the Constitution and the principles of fairness and transparency.
The petitioner has sought a direction to the government to conduct the entire selection process afresh, considering his application.

Crude oil prices moved higher again, with Brent approaching the $100-per-barrel mark and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) also registering gains after the sharp losses recorded earlier in the week. Brent crude was trading at $99.59 per barrel, up $1.30 or 1.32%, while WTI stood at $91.34, gaining $0.82 or 0.91%.
The latest recovery comes after Democrats swept control of both the US House of Representatives and Senate, creating a potential legislative check on President Donald Trump’s administration.
The rebound follows a sharp correction in the previous sessions. On Wednesday, both oil benchmarks suffered losses of more than 8%, their steepest declines in the period covered by the inputs. Brent shed $8.98, or 8.7%, to close at $94.62 per barrel, while WTI dropped $7.97, or 8.3%, to settle at $88.12. Both ended at their lowest closing levels since August 31.
Selling pressure continued on Thursday, pushing Brent below $95 and WTI under $90. Brent futures declined 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 per barrel, while WTI lost 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.
Global refining still feeling the impact of Middle East conflict
The fluctuations in crude prices come as the global oil industry continues to deal with the impact of disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
The outbreak of conflict in the Middle East weighed heavily on refinery operations during the second quarter of 2026, particularly in countries dependent on crude shipments passing through the strait, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).
Global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the preceding quarter, according to data from energy intelligence firm Kpler. Although throughput improved by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, it remained below earlier levels as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.
The impact was particularly visible in Asia. China saw refinery inputs fall by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter, followed by another decline of 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.
India, South Korea and Japan collectively recorded a reduction of more than 1 million b/d in the second quarter. Their combined inputs, however, recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
The Middle East also witnessed a slowdown in refining activity as shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz limited exports of refined petroleum products. Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates each recorded a 0.7 million b/d decline in inputs, while Saudi Arabia saw a reduction of 0.3 million b/d and Iran 0.2 million b/d in the second quarter. Together, the four countries recovered 0.4 million b/d in the third quarter.
Russian oil infrastructure attacks add to supply pressures
Refinery operations in Russia faced a separate setback, with increased attacks on oil infrastructure amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Russian crude oil inputs declined by 0.6 million b/d in the second quarter and fell by another 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.
The reduced refining activity in Russia, alongside disruptions across Asia and the Middle East, added to the pressure on already tight global diesel supplies. These combined disruptions contributed to diesel prices reaching their highest nominal levels on record in September, the EIA said.
The US saw a different trend during the same period. Its refinery inputs rose by 0.5 million b/d in each of the second and third quarters as the country increased refined product exports to make up for shortages in other markets.
However, the improvement in refining activity during the third quarter was not enough to restore global throughput to last year's levels. Inputs remained around 5% lower than in the corresponding period of 2025, despite the gradual improvement in crude oil flows.

stories.headline: Bharti Airtel net profit rises 24% to ₹10,710 crore in September quarter
stories.deck: Bharti Airtel's India revenue grew by 9.4% to ₹42,308 crore
stories.bodyText:
Telecom operator Bharti Airtel on Thursday (November 5, 2026) reported a 24% increase in consolidated profit to ₹10,710 crore in the second quarter ended September 2026, citing higher per-user revenue after a rejig in mobile phone tariffs. The company had a profit of ₹8,651 crore in the same period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing.
Consolidated revenue from operations of Bharti Airtel increased by 16.7% to ₹60,877.5 crore during the reported quarter from ₹52,145.4 crore in the same quarter of the last year. Bharti Airtel's India revenue grew by 9.4% to ₹42,308 crore.
“India mobile service revenue increased by 10.1% YoY, driven by strong customer additions and improved realisation, with Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) expanding to ₹271 in Q2 FY27 from ₹256 in Q2 FY26,” the company said.
Bharti Airtel Executive vice-chairman Gopal Vittal said Africa delivered a standout quarter with 6.7% QoQ constant currency revenue growth.
He said Africa's improving performance is also benefiting from the rollout of Airtel's homegrown technology stack across markets, powering our go-to-market capabilities.
"India business recorded strong revenue growth of 2.7% sequentially. India mobile delivered revenue growth of 3.4% QoQ, backed by our strategy of portfolio premiumisation and winning quality customers," Mr. Vittal said.
Bharti Airtel recorded an 11% increase in global customer base to 69.25 crore during the reported quarter from 62.35 crore in the year-ago period.
Airtel's India customer base increased by about 11% to 49.86 crore. The company's mobile customer base grew by 3.6% to 37.72 crore while home service, which includes fixed line broadband services, grew by about 29% to 1.53 crore.
Mobile data usage per customer on Airtel's network grew by 28.8% to 36.5 GB in the September 2026 quarter from 28.3 GB a year ago. Mr. Vittal said Airtel's postpaid momentum remained strong with record high net customer additions of 12 lakh.
"We added 2.9 million (29 lakh) smartphone data customers with continued improvement of our industry-leading ARPU at ₹271," Mr. Vittal said.
Airtel said strategic focus on strengthening its portfolio proposition led to exceptional performance in the postpaid segment, resulting in record net additions of 12 lakh, taking total base to 3.12 crore. The smartphone data customer base expanded by 1.88 crore over the past year.
Airtel's consolidated capex for the quarter stood at ₹12,467 crore, including India capex of ₹9,908 crore during the reported quarter.
"We continue to strengthen our digital infrastructure and deployed 497 towers and 11,684 mobile broadband base stations during the quarter. Over the past year, network expansion included 5,649 towers and 44,718 km of fiber, significantly enhancing coverage, capacity, and resilience," the company said.
In addition, the company said that it has invested ₹2,826 crore in a strategic land parcel for data centre expansion in India.
The net debt of the company declined by about 14% to ₹1.66 lakh crore from ₹1.94 lakh crore on a year-over-year basis.

stories.headline: Mehli Mistry questions Noel Tata’s citizenship, tax residency status
stories.deck: Mehli Mistry said Noel Tata is an Irish citizen and a holder of a UAE Golden Visa
stories.bodyText:
Mehli Mistry has questioned Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata’s Irish citizenship and tax residency status amid an ongoing legal dispute over his removal from three trusts. Mr. Mistry raised these issues in a submission filed before the Charity Commissioner of Maharashtra (CCM) on Thursday (November 5, 2026), while defending his right to object to change reports filed by Tata Trusts regarding the cessation of his trusteeship.
Tata Trusts had, last month, referred to Mr. Mistry’s U.K. citizenship and UAE tax residency status while challenging his locus standi to file objections to change reports submitted by the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution.
Mr. Mistry has now hit back. In a rejoinder to Tata Trusts’ response, he said Noel Tata is an Irish citizen and a holder of a UAE Golden Visa, and has sought directions from the CCM requiring Tata to file an affidavit clarifying these facts. “If foreign citizenship and overseas residence are to be treated as relevant considerations, they must be examined in relation to the trustee [Tata] with equal rigour. The Trust cannot demand scrutiny of the objector [Mistry] while claiming exemption from the same scrutiny for its own trustee,“ said Mr. Mistry.
Questions over religion and residency have emerged as Mr. Mistry and Tata Trusts differ on the eligibility criteria for trusteeship of the Bai Hirabai Trust. While Mr. Mistry has emphasised the trust deed, which restricts trusteeship to Parsi Zoroastrians, Tata Trusts has argued that these conditions conflict with the original will and codicil governing the trust and should therefore not be relied upon. Tata Trusts did not immediately respond to Mr. Mistry’s latest filing. The matter is now scheduled to be heard by the CCM on December 3.
Mr. Mistry stepped down as a trustee after board members voted against his reappointment to three trusts, including the Sir Ratan Tata Trust. Subsequently, Tata Trusts filed change reports informing the CCM of the end of Mr. Mistry’s tenure. In June, Mistry filed objections to the reports, alleging issues of misgovernance within the trusts.
(The writer is with The Hindu businessline)

briefs.headline: Gold loan defaults see almost 2x rise in 5 months
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Gold loan defaults have nearly doubled in five months even as outstanding balances tripled over three years, pointing to a rise in stress in a rapidly expanding segment of the lending market. Loans overdue by more than 90 days accounted for 0.3% of the portfolio in Aug 2026, up from 0.2% in March 2026. Outstanding gold loans touched a record Rs 22.5 lakh crore in Aug 2026, having tripled since Aug 2023.
TransUnion Cibil's report, Lending Unlocked: Gold Loans, Nov 2026, found that the value of gold loans sanctioned rose 12% year-on-year to Rs 8.2 lakh crore in the three months ended June 2026, despite a 15% decline in the number of loans originated. Around 3.7 crore gold loans were disbursed during the period, while the number of unique borrowers remained broadly stable at 2.4 crore. The divergence suggests that lower origination volumes reflected a shift towards larger-ticket loans rather than reduced borrower participation. According to Bhavesh Jain, MD and CEO of TransUnion Cibil, the number of Gen Z borrowers increased 19% over the preceding five months.

briefs.headline: Wall Street bloodbath: $2.5 trillion wiped out as Nasdaq suffers worst crash in 18 months
briefs.deck: Wall Street faced a dramatic selloff with technology stocks plummeting due to growing concerns about artificial intelligence spending. Investors reevaluated popular AI-related trades after midterm election results suggested potential tougher scrutiny in the industry. The Nasdaq dropped more than 5%, marking its worst session in 18 months and entering correction territory. The selloff spread to…
briefs.bodyText:
Wall Street suffered a massive selloff on Thursday (local time), wiping out a whopping $2.5 trillion in market value in a single day amid AI fears. The fall came as investors pulled back from technology stocks amid growing concerns over heavy artificial intelligence spending and the possibility of tighter industry regulation. The Nasdaq suffered its worst fall in 18 months while the S&P 500 recorded its worst single-day fall since April 2025.
The tech heavy Nasdaq Composite slumped 5.5%, to fall 10% below its recently record high, placing it in correction territory. Nvidia, previously the world’s largest company by market capitalisation, dropped 9.3%, leaving its shares in negative territory for the year. Memory maker SanDisk plunged 22%, while hard drive manufacturer Western Digital lost 17%.
The weakness extended across the wider US market, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, comprising 30 major US companies, falling 1,833 points, or 3.4%, to close at 51,868. The S&P 500 declined between 4.4%, when concerns over US President Donald Trump’s Liberation Day tariffs had rattled markets.
All 11 industry sectors of the S&P 500 ended lower, with seven recording losses of at least 2%. Caterpillar shares dropped 6.4%, JPMorgan Chase fell 4.2%, while UnitedHealth and 3M both declined more than 3%, adding to the pressure on the Dow.
Meanwhile, Wall Street’s VIX, widely known as its ‘fear index’, surged 61% to its highest level since the early weeks of the Iran war, signalling heightened market volatility.
Trump blames ‘Dumocrats’ for Wall Street crash
US President Donald Trump has blamed the sharp market sell-off on the outcome of the midterm elections.
“The Stock Market suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election. Such a sad thing to watch! It took so much work to get us to a level that no one has ever seen before, and then this,” Trump wrote. “Your 401(k)s have, therefore, dropped. Remember, it wasn’t Republicans, it was Dumocrats. Do not fear, however, we will soon, one way or the other, be BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE.”
In a separate post, he added, “The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!”
The remarks come after Democrats secured a landslide win in the 2026 midterm elections, wresting control of Congress from Republicans for the rest of Trump’s term in office.
AI trade under pressure
The sharp decline came as investors reassessed some of the year’s most popular AI-related trades. Growing signs that the artificial intelligence industry could face tougher scrutiny following the US midterm election results have raised concerns about the pace of investment in the sector.
Investors are also positioning for a slower expansion of data centres, putting pressure on chipmakers and companies supplying equipment and infrastructure to the industry.
The sharp fall in equities also prompted investors to move towards safer assets, driving demand for US government bonds. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note slipped to its lowest level since September 9.
The selloff also spread to Asian markets on Friday, with Japan’s Nikkei sliding 6% and South Korea’s Kospi tumbling more than 8% in early trade.
